overview: Spain is a country in south-western Europe, covering most of the Iberian Peninsula. Its capital and largest city is Madrid. In the 1500s Spain built a huge empire in the Americas, which is why Spanish is now one of the most widely spoken languages in the world. Spain returned to democracy after the death of the dictator Francisco Franco in 1975, and it joined what is now the European Union in 1986.

geography.text: Much of Spain is a high central plateau called the Meseta, ringed by mountains such as the Pyrenees on the French border and the Sierra Nevada in the south. Spain has coastlines on both the Atlantic and the Mediterranean. Its territory also includes the Balearic Islands, the Canary Islands off north-west Africa, and the cities of Ceuta and Melilla on the north coast of Africa.

history.text: Spain's history includes centuries of Roman rule and almost eight centuries of Muslim rule in al-Andalus, which ended in 1492 when Granada fell. In the same year, Columbus crossed the Atlantic, beginning a vast Spanish empire in the Americas. After a civil war from 1936 to 1939, General Franco ruled as a dictator until his death in 1975, when Spain became a democracy.

events.title: Muslim conquest
events.text: Armies from North Africa conquer most of the Iberian Peninsula.

events.title: Granada and Columbus
events.text: The last Muslim kingdom falls, and Columbus reaches the Americas.

events.title: The Spanish Armada
events.text: A Spanish invasion fleet sent against England is defeated.

events.title: Civil War
events.text: A three-year civil war ends with General Franco in power.

events.title: Return to democracy
events.text: Franco dies and Spain becomes a democratic monarchy.

events.title: Barcelona Olympics
events.text: Barcelona hosts the Summer Olympic Games.

government.text: Spain is a constitutional monarchy. The King is head of state, and the Prime Minister leads the government with the support of the Cortes Generales, the parliament. Spain is divided into 17 autonomous communities, such as Catalonia and Andalusia, which run their own schools and hospitals. It returned to democracy after General Franco's death in 1975.

economy.text: Spain has one of the largest economies in Europe. It is one of the most visited countries in the world, and tourism is a huge employer. Spain is the world's biggest producer of olive oil and a major exporter of fruit, vegetables, wine and cars. Zara, the clothing brand, is Spanish.

culture.text: Spanish is the world's second most widely spoken native language. Spain is the home of flamenco, paella and tapas, and of artists such as Velázquez, Goya, Picasso and Dalí. Barcelona's Sagrada Família basilica, designed by Antoni Gaudí, has been under construction since 1882.

items.title: Flamenco
items.text: A music and dance style from Andalusia, listed by UNESCO.

items.title: Sagrada Família
items.text: Gaudí's basilica in Barcelona, begun in 1882.

items.title: The Alhambra
items.text: A palace and fortress built by the Muslim rulers of Granada.

sport.text: Football dominates sport in Spain, and Real Madrid and FC Barcelona are two of the most famous clubs in the world. The men's team won the World Cup in 2010 and the women's team in 2023. Spain has also produced tennis greats such as Rafael Nadal, who won the French Open 14 times.

items.title: Rafael Nadal
items.text: Won the French Open a record 14 times.
